# python-broker-client: repairing wide-ranging misbehaviour without a test suite

This is the library an application leans on to hand messages to a broker and to read them back again, and it is getting both halves of that wrong now in a lot of small ways. The repository has received 27 separate undocumented edits. What follows is everything I have been able to observe from the outside, written up by what I was doing rather than by where I guess the problem lives.

Setting up a publishing client and getting messages out goes wrong early. Asking for duplicate suppression while giving the acknowledgement level as the spelled-out word is refused as a contradictory setup, even though that word names exactly the level duplicate suppression requires; the refusal goes away only if I spell the level out as a number instead. Publishing a message that carries a key then behaves as if it had none: the hook that tells the placement strategy to begin a fresh batch fires, and the payload reaches the outgoing batch queue more than once for a single call. Keyless messages go wrong the other way, in that consecutive ones no longer stay on the shard chosen first, each call wanders somewhere else, and after I explicitly rotate the choice for one feed the pinned choice for an unrelated feed moves as well.
